environment.description: Same IoT message handler deployed on EKS pod in cluster eks-prod-iot-2024 (vpc-0def456abc789012). Traffic ingress via AWS Global Accelerator (aga-0x1y2z3a4b5c6d7e8) with endpoint group configured for the NLB (arn:aws:elasticloadbalancing:us-east-1:987654321098:loadbalancer/net/iot-nlb-prod/a1b2c3d4e5f6g7h8). The NLB target group uses IP-mode registration with the pod IPs. A VPC ingress routing table (rtb-0f1e2d3c4b5a6978) is associated with the NLB subnet and routes through a Gateway Load Balancer endpoint (vpce-0a9b8c7d6e5f4321) running Suricata IDS. The critical control: the Global Accelerator endpoint group has client IP address preservation DISABLED, and the NLB has a security group (sg-0q1w2e3r4t5y6u7i) with inbound rules allowing TCP/443 ONLY from the CIDR ranges 203.0.113.0/24 (corporate office), 198.51.100.0/24 (IoT device manufacturing subnet), and 100.64.0.0/16 (carrier-grade NAT for deployed field devices). The pod's Kubernetes NetworkPolicy (netpol/iot-handler-egress) restricts egress to only the kube-dns service on UDP/53 and the device-registry service at 10.0.1.50:8080 - all other egress including to 169.254.169.254 and arbitrary internet hosts is denied by a Calico GlobalNetworkPolicy with order 100 that drops non-matching egress. Pod runs with IMDSv2-only node configuration (HttpTokens: required, HttpPutResponseHopLimit: 1).
